blocks.text: Seth put one hand around the practice bar to straighten it on the stand.
blocks.alt: Seth lifts the heavy practice bar with one hand, surprised by how easily it rises, while Jenny watches.

blocks.text: The whole thing came up.

He caught his balance with the weights hanging level in front of his chest. The plates had not slipped off. Both ends were loaded exactly as they had been that morning, when he had needed two hands and a careful breath to lift them.
Jenny stopped beside the mat.
Seth opened his other hand. He looked at the bar, then at her.
“Was that you?”
She shook her head.
A warmth had passed through him while he reached for the steel. It had been gone before he thought to mention it. Now he held the weight without the familiar trembling in his arm.
He lowered it into the stand. The supports rang.
This time he lifted deliberately, watching the plates clear the hooks. He could feel their weight. He could also feel how much more he had to spare.
Jenny was already moving toward the tape on the floor.
She meant to try the short route they had practiced with Flaming Head watching. A few strides, a turn, a stop inside the square.
Her first step carried her farther than she expected.
blocks.alt: Jenny stops beyond the taped square after an unexpectedly fast practice run, while Seth watches from the side.

blocks.text: The square flashed beneath her. She planted her boots beyond it, arms spread for balance, and stopped with several feet of clear mat still ahead. Her curls swung past her shoulder.
For a moment she stared back at the tape.
Then she laughed.
Seth set the bar down and came toward her.
“Back?” she asked.
He glanced at the heavy plates.
“More than before.”
Jenny walked to the starting mark. She tried again, holding herself well below the speed she could feel waiting. This time she stopped inside the square.
It took almost no effort.
She looked toward the windows.
“He did it.”
Seth followed her gaze.
Beyond the brick buildings, morning sunlight caught the upper windows of Terminal Tower. A gull crossed above the river. Jenny hurried into the operations room and pushed the window open.
She leaned over the sill, searching the sky.
Seth came beside her and drew the curtain clear.
blocks.alt: Seth, Jenny, Billy and Fist wait at the open facility window; the bright sky outside is empty.

blocks.text: Flaming Head had left through this window. They had watched until his light was too small to follow. Jenny had imagined him coming back the same way, looking pleased with himself while they tried to explain how much better they felt.
She waited for his familiar voice.
Traffic moved on the bridge below. Somewhere down the block, a truck backed toward a loading door.
Billy closed his notebook at the desk. He looked from Jenny to Seth, then came to the window. Fist floated across the room to join them.
Seth explained about the weights. Jenny pointed toward the training room and told them what had happened at the stopping mark.
Fist’s eyes widened. He rose above the sill for a better look outside.
Seth listened for Flaming Head too.
His voice had always reached them clearly. Now Seth heard only Jenny breathing beside him.
She called his name aloud.
No answer came.
Billy looked up at her. She kept watching the sky, her hands resting flat on the sill.
They had no way to reach him.
Seth’s arm still felt strong. He wished he had someone to thank.
After a while Billy pulled a chair over to the window. Jenny sat, leaving room beside her for Fist.
Seth stayed standing.
Across the city, Daniel Orkleson pushed his stool away from the stolen vault.
He had tried the torch again before dawn. The groove beside the door was deeper, but the wheel would not turn. Now the torch lay cold on the bench.
Laura had finished the same magazine twice.
Daniel held his gloved hand near the blackened steel, then looked at her.
“It’s cool.”
She put the magazine down.
Jaws drifted closer, keeping clear of the three bright scratches his teeth had left in the locking lug.
Laura crossed the chalk line around the transport frame. She examined the door as though she had been waiting for precisely this opportunity.
The lug projected beside the wheel. Behind it lay all the steel Daniel had failed to cut.
She could still suggest another place for the torch. But Daniel had stepped back and folded his arms. Jaws watched her with delighted expectation.
Laura chose the smallest shot she thought might leave a respectable mark.
A bright bead left her lips.
blocks.alt: Laura’s small plasma shot burns brilliantly into the vault’s lock, startling her while Dork and the floating Jaws watch.

blocks.text: It struck beside the lug.
White light spread across the metal. Laura’s eyes opened wide. The sharp hiss filled the workshop, and a thin stream of molten steel ran down past Daniel’s blackened groove.
She took a step back.
The shot had gone through.
Even before Flaming Head’s capture, she would have expected to work at steel that thick. Now the hole shone deep inside the door, well beyond the ruined locking piece.
Jaws gave an admiring whistle through his iron teeth.
Daniel stared at the cooling metal.
“Why did you let us struggle?”
Laura closed her mouth and made herself look at him instead of the hole.
“You have to choose the right spot.”
She folded her arms before either of them could see her hands.
Daniel waited until the glow had faded. He took the wheel in both gloves and pulled. Something grated inside the door. He changed his grip, tried again, and the damaged mechanism gave.
The bolts slid back.
He pulled the right edge toward him. The heavy door swung on its left hinges, carrying the scorched hole with it.
Shelves filled the strongroom. Bundles of banknotes stood in orderly stacks, their paper bands intact.
Daniel stepped inside.
Laura remained by the chalk line, looking at the depth of the burn. She had meant to hide how little power she had left.
Instead, she had pierced steel that thick with one small shot.
She glanced toward the high windows. Nothing there explained it.
Daniel emerged with a bundle of money in each hand. He set them on the bench beside the Army ray.
Jaws hovered over the open doorway, grinning.
Daniel barely looked at the money again.
He was looking at the tank.
